name: Proper Equivalence Queries Complexity / Teaching Dimension
details: For every finite binary concept class, $\mathrm{Q}_{\mathrm{peq}}(\mathcal H)\geq\mathrm{TD}(\mathcal H)$.
proof: Fix a target $h$ and run an optimal proper equivalence-query learner against any legal counterexample choices.  Record each returned counterexample as its labeled example $(x,h(x))$.  Any $g$ agreeing with all recorded labels admits exactly the same transcript: each recorded $x$ still refutes the corresponding query for $g$.  The learner therefore outputs $h$ on that transcript also when the target is $g$, so correctness forces $g=h$.  The recorded examples are a teaching set for $h$, of size at most the query bound.  Maximizing over $h$ gives $\mathrm{TD}\leq\mathrm{Q}_{\mathrm{peq}}$.
witness_verification: For half-intervals, proper equivalence-query complexity is $\log_2 n$, while teaching dimension is $2$ for $n\geq3$.
